title: Differential Calculus: Cubic Functions, Stationary Points and Concavity
seo_title: Grade 12 Cubic Functions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Determine the co-ordinates of stationary points and points of inflection; sketch graphs of cubic polynomial functions using differentiation to determine the co-ordinate of stationary points, and points of inflection (where concavity changes); also determine the x-intercepts of the graph using the factor theorem and other techniques.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 calculus worksheets: stationary points, maximum and minimum points, increasing and decreasing intervals, points of inflection and concavity of cubic graphs. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Stationary points: f′(x) = 0.
  • f″(x) < 0 at a stationary point: local maximum. f″(x) > 0: local minimum.
  • f is increasing where f′(x) > 0 and decreasing where f′(x) < 0.
  • Point of inflection: f″(x) = 0. Concave up where f″(x) > 0.

Examples

Example

f(x) = x³ − 3x

f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0

x = ±1

Answer: max (−1; 2), min (1; −2)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
f or f′Stationary points: f′(x) = 0.
Max or minCheck the sign of f″.
ConcavityUse f″, not f′.

faq.q: Does every cubic have two stationary points?
faq.a: No, some have one or none.
